reason: The Nguyen-Wood scope entry read the paper and names the two properties the bias argument rests on (entries entering linearly and independently, and quadratically many nonzero coefficients per robust character), and shows both fail for W-type systems, randomized prefixes included (about one random scalar per image column, corrected by its reviewer). This is inapplicability found by a full reading. The code/non-code dichotomy the lead also named was developed separately from Wood 1504.04391 (wood-codes, still continuing at the discriminant step), so no part of the idea is lost.

The expander-core review records the method used in the restriction line (Theorem 4.9 carries every residual argument) and Theorem 3.8 read and found inapplicable to dense clauses, whose locality is a hypothesis of the method. Its only remaining use, the extension lemma from the Miksa-Nordstrom closure, was listed as entry-2026-09-26-expander-core-review:1, which the first pass reopened, so the same source stays queued.

The target of the lead was joint equidistribution of the restricted constants of a block via an upper bound on the normalized permanent of omega^A. lem:swap-decay and cor:dense-shift-equidistribution (both working proofs) give it for every combination far from additive, while near-additive combinations are exactly fixed, which also covers the dense-shared-part case of the adversary. The closing phrase (stalls at the global mechanism) concerns the downstream use, not this lead. It is in effect Developed with no further application.

The target, a base on the forced sparse boards, was proved: lem:relative-criterion and prop:semantic-local-kill are registered working proofs (the verification gate of the closure review calls the criterion a sketch, but the relative review and the registry give it as proved). The open gluing condition 1 notin W_A is carried explicitly by the Miksa-Nordstrom closure lead (expander-core-review:1), which the first pass reopened.

The test proves that over F_3 the only function vanishing off a point has degree 2m, so flat weights cost exactly 2q, and the thread review used this in the replay barrier. Non-flat weights escape because they are not functions of the forms, a hypothesis failure of the theorem. The lead serves lower bounds (barriers), and no current open statement needs a lower bound on weight cost. A1 needs certificates to exist.

The obstruction is a lower bound on exact encodings in the cube variables only, as its own test states. The auxiliary-bit encoding (lem:auxiliary-bit-relaxation, working proof) bypasses it, so it is inapplicable to the encoding the line uses. The integrality line is parked and no open statement relies on the bound.

The closure cites conj:tree-member-saturation, but that refutation used random cylinder sets excluding each point with probability 1/2. The same entry finds that falls fade with density: chains with one-coordinate separators miss falls in 0 of 6 trials at density 0.97. W_RS blocks exclude only about 3^-t of the base, and the original test of the review on real W_RS blocks passed on chains in 4 of 4. So the falsification covers one density regime, not the W_RS setting. The current A3 statement for W_RS (members glued whole, early cross falls conjectured to need a shared piece) is exactly where pair or bounded-cluster saturation would apply.
open_statement: A3 (W_RS: randomized Taylor glue, early cross falls)
next_attempt: Repeat the triple-falls comparison (graded ideal of J1+J2+J3 against the sum of pair saturations) on real W_RS prefix blocks and on cylinder sets at excluded density 3^-t, t=2,3, for chains and triangles at the sizes of triple_falls.m2 and tree_random_sets.m2. If pair saturations generate there, state and try to prove a density-threshold saturation locality that implies the shared-piece conjecture for early cross falls.

reason: Its own closure falsified only the nerve-topology prediction (falls only on cycles). But the Cech/Leray idea was re-raised as a later lead and developed into lem:cover-relative-gluing, thm:sequential-cover-generation and prop:chain-cover-generation (working proofs). Its sheaf and Mayer-Vietoris forms are also carried by later items (design presheaf, contextuality, satisfiable-cover-review:2). The supersession is supported.

Developed into the pullback freeness-inheritance lemma within capacity, then superseded by the Jordan-type lead entry. That entry, reviewer-checked, identifies maximal rank with lem:free-vanishing-tops, the Horace degeneration with lem:hole-splitting plus the open conj:fiber-lattice-freeness, and semicontinuity with thm:generic-top-directness. It also shows that semicontinuity cannot reach F_3-rational families. Restatement plus inapplicability.

Developed into prop:spread-family-level-gap. Its last form, the rank-variety weakening, was closed by a real obstruction: the single-direction failures carry genuine falls (prop:varying-shift-affine-fall, working proof). The Dade idea itself continues in the record: conj:graded-dade (refuted as stated), the open conj:graded-dade-margin, the member-tensor graded Dade review and a later Dade/Carlson lead. So nothing is lost.

The Jordan-type lead entry ran a full cycle with a stated stopping criterion and a reviewer pass. It reduced each of the three forms of the lead to recorded statements and showed that the Horace step leaves the family as far beyond capacity as before. It also showed that semicontinuity fails on F_3-rational points, which the adversary uses. Restatement plus inapplicability found by the attempt.

The test shows the condition of the lead (vectors in no proper subspace) is spanning, now exact in prop:relation-avoidance (working proof). For classes on many tops spanning fails by dimension, so no evasive set exists there. This is a restatement and a dimension-count inapplicability, not a one-step objection.

Developed through four follow-ups: expected Hilbert functions for single tops and pairs proved on one row (group freeness, base-union socle). By prop:batched-splitting (working proof), the many-generator case is the Tor-vanishing open statement itself, which is a restatement. The Froberg idea for the random case of A3 is still carried by the later convergence-review:2 lead, which the first pass reopened.

The identity was developed into thm:cluster-sequential-freeness and prop:linear-transversality (working proofs). These reduce locality to the per-block Tor condition, the open statement of A3 and A2. The identity itself is recorded as prop:overlap-tor. Developed to the point where what remains is the open problem.

The coupled pair is a genuine counterexample to the mechanism of the lead: its cover by two members has a contractible nerve, yet the union is not row-free. So nerve acyclicity cannot certify generation. The algebraic Cech/Mayer-Vietoris form, where the intersection term carries the coupling, is the additivity item (satisfiable-cover-review:2), developed and folded into the cover-generation obstacle. Earlier Cech leads were developed into lem:cover-relative-gluing.

Developed into prop:oriented-cylinder-repair and tested on h-regular coupling graphs in the overdetermined review. The value-side review proves that adversarial overlap graphs exceed every cylinder budget, so no orientation exists. The column-local framework and its (HJ) hypothesis hold only within capacity, while the open part of A1 lies beyond joint capacity. The untried hyperedge (hypergraph-orientation) extension would also live in that framework, so no open statement remains for it.
